I'm reading through the delivery note from Dongguan Precision Housings, a Chinese-headed form numbered SN-260820-788 and dated 2026-08-20, addressed to the Soony Distribution Center in Hamburg under two purchase orders. I'm now going through its line items, starting with the first one for a die-cast statue.

I'm checking the quantities on the two lines: the period in "14.000" reads as a thousands separator in German or Polish, but the document is Chinese, where it's a decimal point, so 14 and 16 pieces make more sense. That also fits the 180 kg gross weight and the 18 total packages matching the 件数 count.

I'm settling on leaving the corrections list empty, since the receiver's signature is a signature rather than an amendment to the note. I'll still record the signature in my observations, and I'm noting the 180 kg gross weight as a document-level figure that doesn't attach to any single line.

I'm filling in the shipment-level details now: the 180 kg gross weight and the carrier, Nordhav Shipping A/S, go in as statements, and the document date is set. The stamped receipt date goes on each line since the stamp covers the whole note. I'm also lining up the two PO numbers and the delivery note number as references, noting the line items as 1 and 2, and marking the status as clean with high confidence.
